units.translation: where since the meter demands an iambic dipody, Klausen conjectured ὁμοιίαν [similar], perhaps rightly, although other examples of this form are not found among the tragedians. To Heimsoeth, ὅμοια [similar things] seems to have been introduced from a gloss in place of ἀντίρροπον [counterbalancing].
In the same sense ἐκ τῶν ὁμοίων [from equal terms].
Your voice utters words similar in form.
In temper like one who speaks most vilely.
I shudder at the goddess who destroys the house, not like the gods.
And indeed the tracks of feet are similar.
From where will you get a prize of equal hand, rich in banquets?
Concerning these things you have come to equal grips.
Again then, like a wrestler, offer the same grip.
And you, like no race of the Sown Men.
For the Nile does not nourish a race similar to Inachus.
A similar vapor, as from a tomb, is fitting.
And if I do not persuade you of anything similar to these things.
But whether you wish to praise or blame me, it is all the same.
Crossing alike over land and sea.
As having been prepared from equal terms to rule over me, having won with his hand.

The dialectal forms have not been made uniform, especially those of the Attic writers. They say ὅμοιος [similar] and γέλοιος [laughable] with the accent on the antepenult, but no longer the words similar to these.
Either send Justice fighting on our side against them, or punish them yourself.
equal grips, instead of exchanges and counter-exchanges
For it is their custom, when they fall together, so that no one may fall upon them in the future, to rise again and grapple in the same posture, which he called the same grip.
the reading, as it seems, is interpolated, about which I have spoken in the Oxford annotation p. 255.
And having been saved, he will rule this land likewise.
To the Danaans and Trojans alike.
And the graces are likewise called glorious lamentation.
And the tomb receives suppliants and exiles alike.
Another would have come likewise to announce these things.
But speak likewise also of your father's mother.
I know how to speak where it is necessary and to be silent likewise.
City and mortal alike would still revere justice.
Thus I wrote for ὁμοκλάν [shout], which is in Strabo p. 470.
He fills the song, a shout that brings on madness.
about which see what Unger collected in Theban Paradoxes p. 323.
When you led Hesione, born of the same father.

the reading, as the meter shows, is shamefully interpolated, which I corrected thus: νῦν δὲ κυανώπιδες θοαὶ νᾶῖς μὲν ἄγαγον, τοτοῖ, νᾶες δ᾽ ἀπώλεσαν, τοτοῖ, ὁμοπτέροισιν ἐμβολαῖς ἠδ᾽ Ἰαόνων χέρες [but now the dark-eyed swift ships brought me, alas, and the ships destroyed me, alas, with simultaneous attacks and the hands of the Ionians], where ὁμοπτέροισιν [with simultaneous wings] used improperly seems to mean simultaneous.
